title: Every endpoint is mapped twice: default-repo and repo-scoped, same handler
statement: A new minimal API route is mapped both as `/api/<resource>` (default repository) and `/api/repos/{repoId}/<resource>` (explicit repository), pointing at the same handler function; the handler resolves the target repository through the shared resolver instead of re-implementing repository lookup.
rationale: Quality Studio is multi-repo; every existing resource endpoint (`tree`, `risk`, `project`, `file`, `inputs`, `guidelines`, ...) follows this exact pairing in `Program.cs`. An endpoint added only in the default-repo form silently breaks for every caller working against a non-default repository, and is easy to miss in review because the app still builds and the default-repo case still works.

good.caption: One handler, two routes, shared repository resolution.

bad.code:
app.MapGet("/api/widgets", (WidgetStore store) => Results.Ok(store.List(DefaultRoot)));
// no /api/repos/{repoId}/widgets route: every non-default repository gets a 404
bad.caption: Only the default-repository route exists.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, grounded in the paired-route convention used across Program.cs.
